# Quality Runner Contract

`scripts/quality-gate.cjs` prints one verdict for one change in any repository. It runs its built-in checks and the commands the repository's committed config names, writes no file and never prints a secret value. A command a manifest implies is suggested and never run, as `quality-config.md` describes. No field and no exit code means pass. Exit 0 says only that no blocker was found and that every required check produced evidence. The acting agent still owns every item in `judgment_required`.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

One reference carries the whole contract a caller needs in order to read a quality run: the CLI, gate values, check states, verdict and envelope grammar, rule ids, reader rules, checker input fields and the dist adapter.

### When to Use

- Running `scripts/quality-gate.cjs` and reading its verdict, exit code or check states
- Choosing a scope, a format or a subset of checks
- Debugging an `ERROR`, `UNVERIFIED` or `NOTHING_CHECKED` result
- Reading what a rule id, a checklist or a surface applies to
- Wiring a configured check or the dist adapter

### CLI

```text
node .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/scripts/quality-gate.cjs [scope] [options]
```

Scope takes one of four flags. Two scope flags in one call are a usage error.

| Flag | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| `--worktree` | The default. Tracked changes against `HEAD`, or against the empty tree before the first commit, plus every untracked file that is not ignored |
| `--base <ref>` | Changes from the merge base of `<ref>` and `HEAD` to the working tree, plus untracked files. No merge base exits 3 with `BASE_NOT_FOUND` |
| `--files <path>...` | The named files only. A path after `--` may start with two dashes. Outside git this is the only scope that runs |
| `--explain <path>...` | Prints `code-quality-explain/v1` for each named file and exits 2, or 3 on a usage error or a missing path. It runs nothing. List several paths after the flag, or repeat the flag once per path |

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--lines changed` | The default. Changed lines come from the new side of `git diff -U0` |
| `--lines file` | Every line of every in-scope file counts as changed |
| `--only <ids>` | Comma-separated check ids, built-in or configured. Every other check reads `SKIPPED_BY_FLAG` |
| `--skip <ids>` | Comma-separated check ids, built-in or configured, that read `SKIPPED_BY_FLAG` |
| `--no-run` | Every spawning check reads `LISTED` with its argv, and a configured check also lists each planned run. In-process checks still run |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | A deadline for each spawned process. The default is 120. A configured check's `timeoutSec` wins for that check. A value under one millisecond rounds up to one millisecond, never down to no deadline |
| `--format json\|text\|envelope` | The default is `json`. `--explain` takes `json` only |
| `--config <path>` | Reads this repository config, relative to the working directory, and records `config.source` as `cli`. A path that does not exist exits 3 with `CONFIG_PATH_MISSING`. `quality-config.md` gives the discovery order and the schema |
| `-h`, `--help` | Prints a plain-text usage to stdout and exits 0: one line per flag, the config discovery order and the exit codes. It reads no config, starts no process and writes nothing. Only an argument before `--` counts, so a file named `-h` can follow the separator |

An unknown flag, a check id that is neither built in nor configured, a missing value or a timeout of zero or less is a `USAGE` error with exit 3.

# Feature Specification: Manually check and refine every skill and mode for readability, layout and structure

<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->
## 1. METADATA

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Level** | 2 |
| **Priority** | P1 |

<!-- ANCHOR:problem -->
## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE

### Problem Statement
The render checks added to `validate_document.py` catch the mechanical defects: joined labels, setext headings, bare URLs, empty overviews, repeated text, misnumbered or misplaced sections. They cannot judge whether a file reads well: whether its intro is a hook, whether a governing decision comes before the steps it governs, whether a wall of prose should be a list, whether items sit in the order a reader needs them. Across 13 skills and 42 modes about 620 docs have never been read for that, and 382 render warnings in other skills sit in a known-debt ledger.

### Purpose
Every skill and mode is read file by file and refined for readability, layout and structure, with no claim changed, and the known-debt ledger shrinks to what remains.

> **Phase-parent note:** This spec.md is the ONLY authored document at the parent level. All detailed planning, task breakdowns, checklists, and decisions live in the child phase folders listed in the Phase Documentation Map below. This keeps the parent from drifting stale as phases execute and pivot.
<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->
## 3. SCOPE

### In Scope
- Per skill: `SKILL.md`, `ROUTER.md`, `README.md`, and every Markdown file under `references/`, `assets/` and `shared/`. A skill with modes gets a hub-and-shared phase for its root files and `shared/`, then one nested phase per mode.
- Per leaf: Luna 6 at xhigh on the fast tier (`cli-codex`, read-only sandbox) lists defects with `file:line` and the exact change. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at high (`cli-pi`, `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`) applies them. Luna re-reads the diff and passes it or sends back a fix list.
- Review rubric, applied in this order: the sk-doc template for the file type; render checks at 0; an intro that is a hook and does not restate the Purpose; Purpose and When to Use first in the overview; a governing decision before the steps it governs; items in the order a reader uses them; paragraphs that pack several mechanisms become lists; indexes list every file they index; no status tokens or authoring history in the body; integer section numbers with related resources last.
- Shrinking `render-known-debt.json` for each skill the program clears.

### Out of Scope
- Changing what a rule, contract or instruction says. Text moves, splits and gets reformatted; every claim survives.
- Changelogs, manual testing playbooks, feature catalogs, benchmarks and tests, which record history or drive tests.
- Rule ids and headings other files link to, unless the leaf updates every inbound link.

### Files to Change

| File Path | Change Type | Phase | Description |
|-----------|-------------|-------|-------------|
| `.skilled/skills/<skill>/` in-scope docs | Modify | Each leaf | Readability, layout and structure |
| `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/render-known-debt.json` | Modify | Each skill | Entries the skill no longer needs |
| `<skill>/changelog/`, `SKILL.md` version | Create, modify | Each skill | Release entry |

- Review rubric, applied in this order: the sk-doc template for the file type; render checks at 0; an intro that is a hook and does not restate the Purpose; Purpose and When to Use first in the overview; a governing decision before the steps it governs; items in the order a reader uses them; paragraphs that pack several mechanisms become lists; indexes list every file they index; no status tokens or authoring history in the body; integer section numbers with related resources last.
- Shrinking `render-known-debt.json` for each skill the program clears.

### Out of Scope
- Changing what a rule, contract or instruction says. Text moves, splits and gets reformatted; every claim survives.
- Changelogs, manual testing playbooks, feature catalogs, benchmarks and tests, which record history or drive tests.
- Rule ids and headings other files link to, unless the leaf updates every inbound link.

# Changelog Version Bump Rules

Concrete four-part version choices and edge distinctions for global component changelogs.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Version bumps apply only to global component changelogs. Packet-local nested changelogs are deprecated, and the existing ones were never versioned this way. This file adds examples to the bump table and auto-detection order in [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) section 4, which stay authoritative.

**When to Use**:

- The SKILL.md bump table is not concrete enough for the change in hand.
- A large change risks being called major when it is not breaking.

---

|---|---|---|---|

description: >-
  Behavior benchmark package for deep-review: eight scenario contracts that
  measure executor-model behavior at the /deep:review command surface under
  realistic prompting. Instantiates the shared framework as its governing
  contract.
trigger_phrases:
  - deep-review behavior benchmark

importance_tier: high

## PURPOSE

This package measures what an executor **model** actually does when the
`/deep:review` command surface is triggered with a realistic user prompt. It is
one of the five `behavior_benchmark` packages carried by the deep-loop workflow
sub-skills; the single-source measurement contract it instantiates is
[../../shared/behavior-benchmark/framework.md](../../shared/behavior-benchmark/framework.md),
which is normative — where this index or a scenario note diverges, that
framework prevails. Each scenario here is a self-contained run contract scored
on the framework's five-dimension rubric and classified into exactly one
terminal bucket.

## SCENARIO TABLE

| ID | Title | Entry | Clarity | Expected | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RVB-001 | Fully-specified :auto run | E1 | C3 | autonomous | 1500000 |
| RVB-002 | Bare command must halt with ONE consolidated setup question | E2 | C2 | question_halt | 300000 |
| RVB-003 | Vague natural ask with no target | E3 | C1 | question_halt | 600000 |
| RVB-004 | Concise natural ask naming the target | E3 | C2 | question_halt | 600000 |
| RVB-005 | Orchestrate-style bounded hand-off | E4 | C2 | autonomous | 600000 |
| RVB-006 | :auto with missing required inputs must fail fast | E1 | C1 | fail_fast | 300000 |
| RVB-007 | Delegation + route-proof under full dimensions | E1 | C3 | autonomous | 1500000 |
| RVB-008 | Absorption probe: asked for the deep process, not an inline review | E3 | C2 | autonomous | 1500000 |

# Benchmark Folder Common Pitfalls

The mistakes that most often make a skill-local benchmark folder drift from its spec packet or break the convention. Check this list when reviewing a drafted `benchmark-report.md` or when a promoted report no longer matches the packet it came from.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Each row names a mistake, why it breaks the skill-local surface, and the correct fix. The two case studies in [case-studies.md](case-studies.md) show real adoptions that avoided these traps; the ALWAYS/NEVER rules and authority hierarchy that back them live in [`../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md) §7.

---

## 2. COMMON MISTAKES

| Mistake | Why It Breaks | Correct Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Promoting before the spec packet ADR is accepted | Skill-local report drifts from the eventual decision | Wait for ADR ratification before authoring `benchmark-report.md` |
| Omitting the load-bearing insight | Future operators miss the finding that matters most | State the non-obvious finding explicitly in Section 1 "What Shipped" and in Section 6 "Findings" |
| Naming folders by doc-authoring date | Folder date no longer matches evidence date | Always use the bench execution date for the folder name |
| Deleting retired benchmark folders | Audit trail is lost | Mark RETIRED in `README.md`; keep the folder |
| Cross-referencing numbers between skills | Stacks differ; numbers are not comparable | Add a "Stack distinction" line in Caveats; link to the sibling README but do not compare figures |
| Creating a new dated folder for a re-run that confirms the winner | Pollutes the index with redundant folders | Update the existing `benchmark-report.md` with a "Re-run YYYY-MM-DD" section |
| Writing a ten-section report without a source.md | Readers cannot find the audit trail | Always author source.md; use the `source-template.md` scaffold |

---

*See [case-studies.md](case-studies.md) for adoptions that avoided these mistakes, and [`../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md) for the authoritative workflow and rules.*

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: README CHECKER COMMAND, LABEL AND COUNT REGRESSIONS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"""Pin the README checkers on slash commands, placeholders, link labels and count claims.

Each case names a mistake a README once carried, or a correct line the
checkers once misread. A stale command, mode, label, deleted file or count
must fail, and a placeholder, shortened link label or rate must not.

Usage: python3 -m pytest -q test_readme_checker_false_positives.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "sk-create-readme" / "scripts"
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPTS))

import check_derived_readme_counts as counts  # type: ignore  # noqa: E402
import check_readme_references as references  # type: ignore  # noqa: E402


def write(path: Path, text: str = "") -> None:
    """Write ``text`` to ``path``, creating any missing parent folders."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def track(root: Path) -> None:
    """Stage every file in the checkout and forget cached listings."""
    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "core.fsmonitor=false", "-C", str(root), "add", "-A"], check=True)
    references._TRACKED_NAMES.clear()


@pytest.fixture()
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """A small checkout with a command tree, a doc folder and a README folder."""
    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "core.fsmonitor=false", "init", "-q", str(tmp_path)], check=True)
    write(
        tmp_path / ".skilled" / "commands" / "create" / "changelog.md",
        '---\nargument-hint: "<target> [:auto|:confirm]"\n---\n# changelog\n',
    )
    write(tmp_path / "docs" / "guide" / "intro.md", "# intro\n")
    write(tmp_path / "pkg" / "run.sh", "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n")
    track(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


def resolve(repo: Path, body: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Check a README holding ``body`` and map each reference to its resolution."""
    readme = repo / "pkg" / "README.md"
    write(readme, body)
    references._TRACKED_NAMES.clear()
    resolutions, missing = references.check_readme(str(readme))
    assert missing is None
    return {item.reference.raw: item for item in resolutions}


def assert_fails(found: dict[str, object], raw: str) -> None:
    assert raw in found, f"{raw!r} was not extracted: {sorted(found)}"
    assert not found[raw].resolved, found[raw].detail


def assert_passes(found: dict[str, object], raw: str) -> None:
    assert raw in found, f"{raw!r} was not extracted: {sorted(found)}"
    assert found[raw].resolved, found[raw].detail


# Slash commands resolve against the command tree.


def test_slash_command_resolves_and_a_missing_one_fails(repo: Path) -> None:
    found = resolve(repo, "Run `/create:changelog`, not `/create:nothing` or `/doc:quality`.\n")

def resolve(repo: Path, body: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Check a README holding ``body`` and map each reference to its resolution."""
    readme = repo / "pkg" / "README.md"
    write(readme, body)
    references._TRACKED_NAMES.clear()
    resolutions, missing = references.check_readme(str(readme))
    assert missing is None
    return {item.reference.raw: item for item in resolutions}


def assert_fails(found: dict[str, object], raw: str) -> None:
    assert raw in found, f"{raw!r} was not extracted: {sorted(found)}"
    assert not found[raw].resolved, found[raw].detail


def assert_passes(found: dict[str, object], raw: str) -> None:
    assert raw in found, f"{raw!r} was not extracted: {sorted(found)}"
    assert found[raw].resolved, found[raw].detail

Overflow depth for authoring a `behavior-benchmark` package. This guide walks the
authoring path end to end and points at the three templates and the normative
framework. It does NOT restate the measurement contract: the five-dimension
rubric, terminal buckets, budget formula, entry-surface and clarity enums, and the
per-package ID-prefix table live once in
[`../../../system-deep-loop/shared/behavior-benchmark/framework.md`](../../../../system-deep-loop/shared/behavior-benchmark/framework.md).
Where this guide and that framework diverge, the framework prevails.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW: WHAT A BEHAVIOR BENCHMARK IS

A behavior benchmark measures what an executor **model** does when a deep-loop
mode's invocation surface is triggered with a realistic user prompt: whether it
dispatches the mode's LEAF agent instead of absorbing the role, whether it halts
for one consolidated setup question when the prompt is under-specified, whether it
respects the mode's invariants, and how long each of those takes relative to a
Claude reference leg. It is a package of run contracts, not a numeric bake-off.

Each behavior benchmark is carried by exactly one deep-loop mode-packet, at
`<mode>/behavior-benchmark/`, and is governed by the single shared framework.
Sibling modes each carry their own package; they share the framework, the runner,
and the scoring so results stay comparable across modes.

### How it differs from an MCP promotion benchmark

The other benchmark family this packet authors — see [`../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md)
sections 3 through 8 — promotes a completed MCP retrieval or runtime bake-off into
a consuming skill's `mcp-server/benchmarks/` folder with a ten-section
`benchmark-report.md`. The two families are distinct and must not be conflated:

| Dimension | MCP promotion benchmark | Behavior benchmark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it measures | Retrieval, quality, runtime, or throughput numbers from a shipped MCP stack | Executor-model behavior at a deep-loop mode's invocation surface |
| Lives at | `<skill>/mcp-server/benchmarks/benchmark-<YYYY-MM-DD>/` | `<mode>/behavior-benchmark/` |
| Central artifact | Ten-section `benchmark-report.md` plus `source.md` | `behavior-benchmark.md` index plus per-scenario contracts plus a baseline |
| Governing contract | The report contract in `../SKILL.md` | The shared `framework.md` |
| Evidence location | The dated folder is the curated surface; audit trail in the spec packet | The package holds the contract; run evidence lands in the executing spec-packet phase |

If the task is promoting MCP numbers, use the MCP-promotion path in `../SKILL.md`.
If the task is specifying executor behavior for a deep-loop mode, use this guide.

---

=====
# Benchmark Adoption Case Studies

Two adoptions teach the format from opposite ends: one promoted into a live skill, one deliberately kept archived. Read them when modeling a new benchmark folder or deciding whether a provisional run is ready to promote.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Each case study records what triggered the adoption decision, the load-bearing insight the folder had to surface, and the lesson for the next author. Case study 1 is a clean promotion backed by many ADRs; case study 2 is a correctly-formatted run that was deliberately never promoted because its headline was a single-run signal. Neither folder is on disk any more, so both read as narrative. The lesson outlives the artifact, which is itself worth noticing when you decide what to write down.

---

## 2. CASE STUDY 1: TEXT-EMBEDDER BAKE-OFF (May 17, 2026)

The folder lived in the memory MCP server's skill tree and went with that server when it was decommissioned. What follows is the narrative, not a link.

=====

The mistakes that most often make a skill-local benchmark folder drift from its spec packet or break the convention. Check this list when reviewing a drafted `benchmark-report.md` or when a promoted report no longer matches the packet it came from.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Each row names a mistake, why it breaks the skill-local surface, and the correct fix. The two case studies in [case-studies.md](case-studies.md) show real adoptions that avoided these traps; the ALWAYS/NEVER rules and authority hierarchy that back them live in [`../SKILL.md`](../../SKILL.md) §7.
